result:
If I could flip one global switch, I’d make high-quality education freely available to everyone, everywhere, for life.

Why that choice:

1. Foundation for everything else  
   • Health, economic opportunity, civic engagement, scientific progress—all rise with education.  
   • It equips people to solve their own local problems rather than waiting for outside fixes.

2. Compounding returns  
   • Each learner can teach others, so the benefit snowballs across generations.  
   • Better-educated societies tend to value evidence, tolerance, and collaboration, which reinforces peace and innovation.

3. Resilience in a changing world  
   • Technology, climate, and job markets evolve quickly; continuous learning is the best safety net.  
   • An informed population is harder to manipulate and more capable of holding power accountable.

4. Moral rationale  
   • Talent is distributed randomly; opportunity shouldn’t be.  
   • Giving everyone the tools to understand and shape their world feels like the fairest single lever to pull.

No single change fixes everything, but universal, lifelong learning comes closest to unlocking the rest.
